claims: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor (MD or DO).
A psychiatrist specializes in mental health, including substance use disorders.
Psychiatrists diagnose mental illnesses.
Psychiatrists treat mental illnesses.
Psychiatrists help prevent mental illnesses.
Psychiatrists are qualified to prescribe medications.
Psychiatrists are qualified to order lab tests.
Psychiatrists are qualified to conduct physical exams to assess the link between physical and mental health.
Psychiatrists use the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) to diagnose conditions.
Psychiatrists use the DSM-5 to create treatment plans.
Psychiatrists often combine medication management with psychotherapy.
Psychiatrists prescribe psychiatric medications for illnesses like schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, and anxiety.
Psychiatrists monitor psychiatric medications for illnesses like schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, and anxiety.
Some psychiatrists are trained in electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).
Some psychiatrists are trained in transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS).
Some psychiatrists are trained in ketamine therapy.
Psychiatrists work in private practices, hospitals, clinics, emergency rooms, nursing homes, and forensic settings.
Psychiatrists focus on biological, chemical, and psychological aspects.
Psychologists have PhD/PsyD.
Psychologists focus on psychotherapy, psychological testing, and behavior change.
Psychologists typically do not prescribe medication.
Becoming a psychiatrist requires roughly 12 years of training.
Becoming a psychiatrist includes a four-year bachelor’s degree.
Becoming a psychiatrist includes four years of medical school.
Becoming a psychiatrist includes a four-year residency in psychiatry.
